svg.text: Everything inside the 300 x 200 x 130 box, lid off, seen from the front. Microphone and 4G antenna are both internal. Cable numbers match the schedule.
A Interior layout and cable routing
on a shelf above the battery
Only 3 glands now, all on the UNDERSIDE. The mic port is a 5 mm hole in the wall.
2 x 4 mm2 solar cable, MC4 pigtail pair
2 x 2.5 mm2 + inline 15 A blade fuse + ring terminals
USB-A to micro-USB (check the 4 Mini, it may be USB-C)
6-core Dupont on I2S, via a stacking header
Gone with the whip: the lavalier and its sound card, the CRC9 pigtail, the SMA extension and the antenna.
Also needed: ferrules, ring terminals, heatshrink, UV ties, nylon standoffs, a battery strap, acoustic membrane.
The buck and the probes both hang on the MPPT's LOAD output, not on the
battery, so Victron's low-voltage disconnect protects the cells and the probes
stop drawing power through the fourteen hours the node is asleep.
The Witty Pi sits on the GPIO header, so the microphone needs a stacking
header underneath it to reach the I2S pins. Check this before ordering.
Both probes leave the factory on Modbus address 1. Re-address one to 2
(register 07D0) on the bench, or they collide and neither reads.
SEN0600 exposes moisture (0000H) and temperature (0001H) only, so it uses
the sen0600 profile, which reads two registers rather than three.
Probe wire colours are not published. Meter them before splicing: the family
convention is brown +V, black GND, yellow A, blue B.
Leave the galvanised steel mounting plate out of the box. A 4G antenna radiates through polycarbonate for a few dB of loss, but a steel plate beside it detunes the antenna and
puts nulls in the pattern. Mount the boards on a cut sheet of 3 mm plastic instead, which also removes the need to isolate anything from the plate.
Nothing here is verified on hardware yet. Meter every colour and check every connector against the part in your hand before you cut anything.
